candidates.rights_reasoning: The Library of Congress states that it is aware of no copyright in the collection and that the manuscripts were generally written by U.S. Government employees whose works are not copyrightable in the United States. ([loc.gov](https://www.loc.gov/resource/wpalh2.29091808/?st=pdf&utm_source=openai))
candidates.story_fit_reason: The interview centers on Mrs. Jane Lee Smith’s recollections of her parents crossing the plains, including a vivid episode in which cattle unexpectedly line up for a confrontation with the family ox, Brindy. ([loc.gov](https://www.loc.gov/resource/wpalh2.29091808/?st=list&utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: The source is a transcription of recollections about an earlier generation, and the Library of Congress warns that privacy and publicity rights may still apply.

candidates.title: The Barber Who Was Also the Town Dentist
candidates.rights_status_quote: The Library of Congress is not aware of any copyright in the documents in this collection. As far as is known, the documents were written by U.S. Government employees. Generally speaking, works created by U.S. Government employees are not eligible for copyright protection in the United States, although they may be under copyright in some foreign countries.
candidates.rights_reasoning: The Library of Congress identifies the collection as containing documents with no known copyright and explains that works created by U.S. Government employees are generally ineligible for U.S. copyright protection. ([loc.gov](https://www.loc.gov/resource/wpalh2.20040609/?st=text&utm_source=openai))
candidates.story_fit_reason: Clara Fergusson’s life-history material offers a sharply focused small-town situation: one barber serves simultaneously as dentist, flag-raiser, and Fourth-of-July cannon operator in old Albuquerque. ([tile.loc.gov](https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/mss/wpalh/wpalh-20040609/wpalh-20040609.pdf?utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: The narrative includes culturally sensitive descriptions of Mexican and Indigenous religious practices, so adaptation should avoid caricature.
